title: Language models missed more requirements with little wording in common with the final request
summary: Across 405 CL-bench Life tasks, direct answers from four language models passed 67.4% of rubric criteria with low wording overlap with the final request, compared with 81.1% of higher-overlap criteria. The analysis uses word overlap as a proxy and does not establish that wording alone caused the difference.
ai_technology: GPT-6 Luna; Kimi K3; Grok 4.7; GLM-5
organization: The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Macao Polytechnic University; The Hong Kong Polytechnic University

source_review.scope: v1 CL-bench Life task corpus description, lexical rubric groups and direct-answer results

evidence.tested: The study grouped 5,333 classifiable rubric criteria by overlap with the final request. The evaluators assessed individual outputs under the benchmark rubric.
evidence.unknown: Groups can differ in underlying difficulty and scoring criteria. Rubrics are nested within tasks, and the result does not establish effects in live workflows.
evidence.ai_role: Four frozen language models generated corpus-task answers. A rubric judge scored outputs from the same benchmark before testing the proposed harness.
